title: Hold a cable's stripped end in a crimper's terminal with one hand while the other presses the lever to crimp it
instruction: Pick up the cable and push its bare end straight into the terminal's barrel in the crimper with one hand, and hold it there while the other presses the crimper's lever down until it closes; then let the lever spring open.
context: Crimping terminals onto cables is everyday work in wiring-harness and electronics assembly, including the power and network cabling of data centres. It is still done largely by hand: the cable has to be held straight in the terminal at the right depth while the tool closes, or the crimp is bad.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A fixed bench crimper on the centre line, 30 cm forward. In its die sits a copper ring terminal whose barrel, 13 mm across inside and 16 mm long, points toward the arms, its axis 4.5 cm above the table, with a flared lead-in 2 cm across in front of its mouth. Its lever is hinged 6.5 cm left of the barrel and reaches right; its red rubber grip is 14.5 cm right of the centre line. A spring holds the lever 12 degrees open (the grip 4.4 cm above closed); holding it closed takes about 5 N on the grip. (2) A loose stiff cable, 16 cm long, 8 mm across and 30 g, its last 12 mm stripped to bare copper 6 mm across. It lies on two fixed V-rests along the forward direction, 12 cm left of the centre line, its bare tip 26.5 cm forward and 4.5 cm above the table. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial. The crimp: the moment the lever first closes (within 1.5 degrees). A good crimp: then the bare end 6 to 14 mm into the barrel (at least half its 12 mm of copper in, at most 2 mm of insulation) and the cable within 8 degrees of the barrel's axis. Released: the lever back open at least 10 degrees and the gripper that pressed it (its fingertip centre, TCP) at least 4 cm from the grip. 1.0: a good crimp, released; 0.5: any crimp with the bare end in the barrel; 0.25: the bare end pushed at least 6 mm into the barrel at some point; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held with the lever and the cable still for 1 s.
reset_notes: Fit a fresh terminal in the crimper's die and lay a fresh stripped cable on its rests.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: the crimp is an event. When the lever closes, the task file reads where the cable's bare end is and fixes the cable to the crimper there (a fixed joint), as the crimped barrel would; the barrel does not deform. The cable is a stiff rod, and the lever a hinge with a return spring. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
